Title: Briefs 09–10 | Monte Carlo Physics

LEFT CARD HEADER: BRIEF 09 — BOUNDED 2D ISING FERROMAGNET
Left visual: a clean illustrated square spin lattice with small arrows/spins, a few coherent domains, and a temperature cue; show it as an educational diagram, not a decorative generic atom image.

LEFT CARD — CONTEXT + OBJECTIVE: A 2D lattice of interacting spins represents a simple ferromagnet. Investigate how temperature changes domain structure, magnetisation and energy, and identify what the finite simulation can support.

LEFT CARD — POSSIBLE REALISM DIMENSIONS: Temperature, lattice size, boundary condition, coupling strength, initial state, equilibration, random seed and finite-size effects.

LEFT CARD — LIKELY INFORMATION: Lattice size, interaction parameter or energy scale, temperature range, supplied or AI-assisted scaffold, initial state and any reference behaviour actually supplied.

LEFT CARD — BOUNDARY QUESTIONS: How many updates are enough? Is the lattice large enough? Does the initial state matter? Are edge effects material? Is a sharp transition claim defensible?

RIGHT CARD HEADER: BRIEF 10 — FIELD OF AN IRREGULAR CHARGED BODY
Right visual: an illustrated irregular charged body or plate with distributed charge markers and field lines sampled toward observation points; make the geometry visibly non-uniform, but do not show equations or a prescribed algorithm.

RIGHT CARD — CONTEXT + OBJECTIVE: A charged body has irregular shape and non-uniform charge density. Use random samples to estimate the electric field at selected observation points and compare the result with a simpler reference case.

RIGHT CARD — POSSIBLE REALISM DIMENSIONS: Geometry, charge-density variation, near-field behaviour, observation-point location, sample distribution, sample count, and singular or excluded regions.

RIGHT CARD — LIKELY INFORMATION: Body geometry or bounding region, charge-density description, observation points, unit and scale information, sample counts and any symmetric reference case actually supplied.

RIGHT CARD — BOUNDARY QUESTIONS: Is the sampling distribution unbiased? How does sample count affect spread? How close can a point be to the source? Is a 2D approximation defensible? When is the estimate converged?

FOOTER: Make each random trial physically meaningful; report mean, spread, sample-size effect and a reproducible check.
